note: Pascal wrote in French, so no Pascal sentence is back-translated from Trotter's English: every quotation is his own wording from the Brunschvicg text in pensees.fr.json (Life of Pascal for « depuis l’âge de dix-huit ans… sans douleur », the sick-child episode and « Que Dieu ne m’abandonne jamais ! »). Where the English trims a fragment, the French keeps the matching run of Pascal's words; two silent corrections of the source transcription: « suffit » for « suffît » (roseau pensant, B. 347) and « à force » for « a force » (B. 536). The attribution drops the Trotter credit and says Pascal is quoted from his original French.

The Memorial (ch. 1) is not in the repo's French files: « FEU. Dieu d’Abraham, Dieu d’Isaac, Dieu de Jacob, non des philosophes et des savants. Certitude. Certitude. Sentiment. Joie. Paix. Dieu de Jésus-Christ. » is original wording from memory, needs checking (punctuation follows the usual Brunschvicg/Lafuma layout).

Archaic words kept inside Pascal's quotations get a short bracketed gloss in the narration: goujat/crocheteur (ch. 4), imbécile = faible (ch. 6), « prendre croix » (ch. 9); « l’expérience nous pipe » is glossed in-line (ch. 3). In ch. 9 the wager's practices follow Pascal (« prendre de l’eau bénite, faire dire des messes »), not the English's 'attending Mass'.

The KJV epigraphs are replaced by Louis Segond (1910) verbatim, cited with Segond numbering: Psalm 46:10 = Psaume 46:11, Psalm 42:1–2 = Psaume 42:2–3, Psalm 8:3–4 = Psaume 8:4–5. Partial epigraphs (Exodus 3:6, Joshua 24:15, Matthew 22:37, Matthew 26:38) quote the matching Segond portion; Joshua 24:15's fragment is capitalised (« Choisissez »). Indirect echoes in the narration are self_rendered.

Title « Pensées (Pour ados) » (19 chars) follows the shipped « (Pour ados) » pattern; narration in passé simple for the biography, « tu » for the reader as in a-retrospect-teens.fr. AI-translated in-session; awaiting native review.
